subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw implement these anti-drift guards as part of one structured lifecycle/process-events contract, or as a standalone runtime enforcement layer with its own feature flag and timers?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the durable fix defines public runtime, protocol, session, telemetry, and possibly config semantics; automation cannot safely choose that product contract or the false-positive tolerance.

options.title: Unify With Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Fold artifact evidence, blocker escalation, post-green closure, and no-progress detection into one additive run lifecycle/process-events contract shared with related progress-state work.

options.title: Standalone Guard Layer
options.body: Implement a separate `ENFORCEMENT_GUARDS_V1` layer with persisted guard state and timers, accepting the extra compatibility and duplicate-state review burden.

options.title: Keep Current Narrow Guards
options.body: Treat strict-agentic retries and post-compaction loop aborts as sufficient for now, leaving this issue open only for future telemetry or docs refinement.

recommendation.title: Unify With Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Fold artifact evidence, blocker escalation, post-green closure, and no-progress detection into one additive run lifecycle/process-events contract shared with related progress-state work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest product-contract history on strict-agentic execution and structured execution item events, which are the closest existing design surfaces.
